evals.name: design-payouts-endpoint
evals.prompt: I'm building a POST /api/v1/payouts endpoint in our Next.js app. It can fail in a few ways: the user's connected bank token has expired, the requested amount exceeds their daily payout limit, and sometimes our payment provider (a vendor called Sequra) rejects it with its own error code. Design the JSON error response body the API should return for these cases.
evals.expected_output: An issues array with one entry per failure, each having a single namespaced issue code in {domain}.{class}.{reason} form (e.g. payout.unauthorized.token_expired) and NO separate type field, plus severity, correlationId, dateTime; the Sequra rejection surfaced via a thirdParty object; descriptive string codes not numeric; links and message where useful.

evals.name: review-adhoc-error
evals.expected_output: Critique identifying the ad-hoc shape, numeric/opaque code, lack of correlationId, no path forward; recommends a unified issues array with a single descriptive namespaced string code ({domain}.{class}.{reason}, no separate type field), severity, correlationId, message title/detail, and links. Shows a concrete before/after.

evals.name: unify-rest-and-webhooks
evals.prompt: Our REST API returns errors one way but our webhooks deliver failures in a totally different shape, and our React frontend has to special-case both. How should we make error handling consistent across responses and webhooks, and how would we consume the unified shape in the frontend?
evals.expected_output: Recommends one consistent issues shape reused across responses and webhooks; explains the consistency principle; provides a React consumption example splitting errors vs warnings by severity and surfacing correlationId; tolerates unknown issue codes and parses the class from the code rather than a separate type field.

evals.name: design-order-status-lifecycle
evals.prompt: We're modelling the lifecycle of an order in our API. Right now we have a single `status` string that can be `created`, `paid`, `payment_failed`, `shipped`, or `delivered`, and we fire a webhook on every change. But a failed payment can be retried, and the frontend keeps having to special-case `payment_failed` to know what to show the user and whether they can try again. How should we model and name the order's states and the events?
evals.expected_output: Recommends drawing the state machine first; separates the event (what happened, past-tense verb on the webhook envelope) from the status (where the resource is, a persistent {domain}.{state}.{substate} string) from the issue (why / what to do); points out payment_failed conflates a state with a failure reason and that failure should loop back to a recoverable state (e.g. unpaid) rather than be terminal; names states for the PRESENT CONDITION (what the resource is now) rather than the obligation/next step — avoids pending and requires_* naming; discusses enum-vs-parseable-string trade-off and the shared grammar with issue codes.

evals.name: dashboard-endpoint-vs-resources
evals.prompt: Our React dashboard has a customer detail screen that shows the customer, their last 5 invoices, their outstanding balance, and a formatted 'next action' label. Right now the frontend calls GET /customers/{id}, then GET /customers/{id}/invoices, then computes the balance and the label itself. It feels chatty and the logic is duplicated in our mobile app. Should we just add all those fields to GET /customers/{id}? How should we structure this?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes view/presentation endpoints from canonical resource endpoints; warns against accreting UI-specific/derived fields (balance, formatted label) onto the canonical /customers/{id} resource because it couples the platform API to one screen; recommends a dedicated view/BFF endpoint that aggregates and formats for that screen, owned by the frontend, sitting over the resource layer; notes writes still go to resource endpoints; may reference BFF/GraphQL/CQRS.

evals.name: ambiguous-auth-schemes
evals.prompt: Our API docs just say 'authenticate with your API key in the Authorization header'. Internally we have a normal access token and a 'stepped-up' token (after the user does an extra verification) that's required for sensitive endpoints like moving money — but it's technically the same token type. Integrators keep getting confused about what to send where. How should we present auth?
evals.expected_output: Treats security schemes as discrete, named contracts each endpoint maps to exactly one of; separates the credential's implementation from the consumer-facing scheme (make the API-key-to-header transform explicit); explains that the normal vs stepped-up token are functionally different schemes even though technically the same token, and each endpoint should declare which it requires; recommends modelling this explicitly (e.g. OpenAPI named securitySchemes + per-operation security).

evals.name: 3ds-authentication-state
evals.prompt: We have a payments API and we're adding 3D Secure. When a charge needs the cardholder to complete a 3DS challenge, the payment pauses until they do it. I was going to add a `requires_action` status (copying Stripe) and have the frontend check for it to know when to pop the challenge. The status field is currently an enum: `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed`. How should I model the 3DS-pause state and tell the frontend to show the challenge?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on requires_action / pending as status names because they describe the consumer's next step (future tense) rather than the resource's present condition; recommends a present-condition status like authentication_required (lead with the missing thing, not requires_authentication) and putting the actionable part (the challenge link, the do-this) in an issue, not the status; notes failure should loop back not be terminal; may suggest a parseable {domain}.{state} string over a brittle enum.

evals.name: multi-actor-onboarding-lifecycle
evals.prompt: We're modelling a business onboarding (KYB) flow as a status field. The applicant fills in disclosures (which can be not started, partially done, or complete), then we review it (which is either in progress, approved, or rejected). Sometimes the ball is in the applicant's court, sometimes in ours. Our dashboard's main job is showing our ops team which applications are waiting on us vs waiting on the customer. I was thinking statuses like `kyb.review` for in-review and `kyb.review.approved` / `kyb.review.rejected` for the outcomes. Does that work?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a bare kyb.review parent that ALSO has children (approved/rejected) breaks prefix matching — a parent segment must be a pure container (every state carries a leaf, e.g. review.in_progress/review.approved/review.rejected) or a flat state with no children, never both, and it's worst when children are terminal; explains the middle segment is an axis you choose, and since the dashboard's job is 'who owns the next move' it should group by actor (e.g. awaiting_user vs in_review/awaiting_us) so that's a one-segment prefix match; states named for present conditions.
